title: Docs: add Regulated Workloads section + link Private/VPC reference architecture and Security FAQ addenda
author: Kira Thompson
description: Summary: Adds a new “Regulated workloads” section in the docs under Security & Compliance and wires in links to (1) the Private/VPC reference architecture page and (2) the FinServ + Healthcare security FAQ addenda. This is intended to support the regulated-workloads ABM pilot by making security-forward material easier to discover while keeping claims aligned with current product posture. Scope: New landing page + navigation entry, short overview content (deployment modes, auditability, residency/retention framing), and a “What we can share” callout for security artifacts (SOC 2 report, questionnaire responses) to avoid over-sharing in public docs. Notes: Security review requested several wording changes around retention, audit logs, and KMS/HSM phrasing; those edits are included (see conversation). Testing: local `pnpm test` + `pnpm lint` and preview deploy verified; links validated via build-time link checker. Follow-ups: The reference architecture page content will continue to evolve as Private installer/networking guidance hardens; this PR keeps the content high-level and points to Solutions Engineering for environment-specific details.

docs(security): add links to security FAQ addenda with 'available upon request' language
docs(architecture): link Private/VPC reference architecture and clarify responsibility boundaries
chore: fix link checker failures and normalize headings
files_changed: content/security-compliance/index.mdx (add callout + link to regulated workloads)
content/private-deployments/reference-architectures/private-vpc-regulated.mdx (new page: high-level reference architecture + diagrams + shared responsibility notes)
content/security-compliance/audit-logging.mdx (add cross-links; clarify export formats as 'supported options' not guarantees)
README.md (contributor note: security/compliance content requires Security/GRC review)
checks: vercel/preview — pass (Preview URL posted in PR thread)
review_conversation: Elliot Price (Docs lead): “Overall structure makes sense and matches the ABM needs. Two requests: (1) keep the landing page focused (avoid repeating all of Security & Compliance), (2) add a small ‘shared responsibility’ section near the top of the reference architecture page so customers don’t assume Redwood runs their SIEM/KMS.”

Kira Thompson (author): “Done. I tightened the landing page to be an index + pointers, and added a ‘Shared responsibility’ block to the reference architecture (Redwood control plane vs customer environment + who owns SIEM export plumbing).”

Dr. Aisha Rahman (CISO): “We need to adjust a few phrases before this goes public: - Please avoid ‘we do not store prompts/outputs’ as an absolute statement. Replace with approved residency/retention language and explicitly scope to deployment mode. - Do not imply HSM support is universal; use ‘KMS integrations and HSM-backed keys where supported by your KMS/HSM provider’ and keep it ‘configuration dependent’. - SOC 2 report should be ‘available under NDA’ not directly linked. - Replace ‘HIPAA-ready’ with neutral language (‘supports regulated workloads; will sign BAA where applicable through the enterprise process’).”

Kira Thompson (author): “Acknowledged. I updated the retention section to the approved phrasing (‘data handling varies by deployment mode and configuration; we can provide details during security review’), changed the KMS/HSM sentence to the narrower wording, removed any direct SOC 2 report link and replaced with ‘request via security review’, and removed ‘HIPAA-ready’ in favor of neutral language.”

Marcus Lin (Security Eng): “On the audit logging bullet list: avoid enumerating specific SIEM vendors unless we have committed integrations. Also, ‘real-time’ is too strong; please say ‘near-real-time’ or ‘streaming/export options’. Lastly, the reference architecture diagram caption says ‘customer-managed HSM’—should be ‘customer-managed KMS/HSM’ and only as an integration point.”

Kira Thompson (author): “Updated: removed vendor names, changed ‘real-time’ → ‘streaming/near-real-time export options’, and corrected diagram caption to ‘customer-managed KMS/HSM integration point (optional)’. Also added note that exact export formats are configured per deployment.”

Olga Petrov (GRC): “Please add a short ‘Evidence we typically provide’ section: SOC 2 (under NDA), pen test summary (under NDA), RBAC/SSO description, audit log examples, and a note that customer questionnaires are handled via Security/GRC. This helps align expectations and reduces ad-hoc requests.”

Kira Thompson (author): “Added a ‘Common evidence requests’ section with that list and a pointer to contact Security/GRC. Also added wording that responses may require NDA and are provided through the enterprise process.”

Soojin Lee (Product Marketing): “Love the flow. One request: the ‘Hosted → Dedicated → Private’ sentence reads like a promise of seamless migration. Can we soften it to ‘a path many teams take’ and emphasize evaluation/rollout planning?”
Kira Thompson (author): “Adjusted to ‘a common path’ + added a sentence about planning and validation (security review + POC) before moving into Private.”
Dr. Aisha Rahman (CISO): “Final pass looks good. Approved with the current phrasing.”
Elliot Price (Docs lead): “Approved. Please make sure we keep the reference architecture page labeled ‘high-level’ and route implementation-specific questions to SE.”
release_notes: Docs: Added a Regulated Workloads section with curated links to Private/VPC reference architecture and security/compliance artifacts request flow (SOC 2, audit logging, residency/retention).
